programme.title: Originals: Ronaldo Nazário - El Presidente
programme.desc: Im September 2018 wird Ronaldo Nazario de Lima der Hauptanteilseigner von Real Valladolid. Der zweimalige Weltfußballer investiert einen Millionenbetrag aus seiner eigenen Tasche - ein ungewöhnlicher Schritt für einen ehemaligen Profi. Der Weltmeister von 2002 steckt viel Herzblut in den Klub und pflegt ein enges Verhältnis zu seinen Spielern, die er nach einem erfolgreichen Abstiegskampf zu einer Party in seiner Villa auf Ibiza einlädt.

programme.title: Originals: Ronaldo Nazário - El Presidente
programme.desc: Nach dem Klassenerhalt und ausgiebigen Partys auf Ronaldos Boot steht der Klub trotzdem vor großen Problemen. Die spanische Polizei ermittelt wegen möglicher Spiel-Manipulationen. Sieben Valladolid-Spieler werden befragt und der ehemalige Kapitän muss ins Gefängnis. Zusätzlich verlässt Topstürmer Sergi Guardiola den Klub. Sportlich läuft es aber gut, allen voran beim Innenverteidiger-Youngster Mohammed Salisu. 26 Jahre zuvor war der jetzige Klubpräsident selbst ein großes Talent. Weltmeister-Mannschaftskollege Roberto Carlos erinnert sich an Ronaldos Anfänge bei Cruzeiro Belo Horizonte.

programme.sub-title: Parallelen zu Virgil van Dijk? - Episode 1
programme.desc: Er hat ambitionierte Ziele, als Talent sieht sich Jonathan Tah nicht mehr. In der Entwicklung gibt es Parallelen zum jungen Virgil van Dijk. Jonas größte Fortschritte folgten immer auf Rückschläge. Mit 17 schon Bundesliga-Stammspieler, dann plötzlich außen vor.

programme.title: Jona 99 - Mehr Sein als Schein
programme.desc: Das Sportliche gerät 2020 schnell in den Hintergrund. Eine Pandemie stellt alles auf den Kopf. Jona überdenkt während der Corona-Pause vieles. Er ist Geschäftsmann und bildet sicht auf verschiedenen Ebenen weiter. In Jonathan Tah steckt viel mehr als nur ein herausragender Fußballer, das wissen vor allem seine engen Freunde zu schätzen.

programme.desc: Contestants compete to win cash prizes in a mash-up of two game show formats, first by trying to match celebrities' answers to fill-in-the-blank questions and then by choosing to either agree or disagree with celebrities' answers to trivia questions.

programme.title: Family Feud
programme.desc: In this original version of iconic game show "Family Feud," actor Richard Dawson plays host to two teams, each comprised of five family members, who try to match the answers given to survey questions asked to groups of people (typically 100 people in the group). The family that wins the game by being the first to reach a certain point total, either 200 or 300 depending on the rules at the time, advances to the bonus round, called Fast Money, for a chance to win thousands of dollars by answering more survey questions.

programme.title: Temptation
programme.desc: Host Rossi Morreale welcomes three contestants who accumulate cash winnings by correctly answering a series of questions about pop culture and current events. At the end of each show, the winner is the player who has ammassed the most money, but throughout the game contestants are tempted to use their winnings on high-end prizes they can buy at incredible bargain prices.

programme.title: Press Your Luck
programme.desc: Contestants try to answer trivia answers correctly to collect spins on a gameboard, where they can win cash and prizes. Unless, of course, they land on a "Whammy," which takes away the player's loot. The contestant with the most accumulated cash and prizes at the end of the show is the winner.

programme.title: Super Password
programme.desc: Like the 1960s version, two contestants, each teamed with a celebrity partner, compete in a word-association game. One player tries to guess a word based on clues offered by his or her partner. The game is timed, and if the clue-giver inadvertently says part of the word, a buzzer sounds and that round is lost. The team with the most points at the end of the round gets to go on to a fast-paced bonus round called Cashword.

programme.title: The Price Is Right
programme.desc: "Come on down!" "The Price Is Right" -- hosted by Bob Barker until 2007 and Drew Carey thereafter -- features a wide variety of games and contests with the same basic challenge: Guess the prices of everyday (or not-quite-everyday) retail items. Four contestants, all of whom are seated in one of the wildest audiences in daytime game-show history, are called to the stage to play a preliminary pricing round. That winner joins the host on stage for one of more than 70 different pricing games. After three such games, the contestants spin a big wheel -- hoping to get as close to $1 as possible -- in the "Showcase Showdown." The two highest winners of that round advance to the final, where prizes could be cars or roomsful of furniture. A trio of models presents the prizes.

programme.title: Card Sharks
programme.desc: This show from legendary Mark Goodson-Bill Todman Productions features two contestants trying to predict answers to survey questions for the opportunity to play a game with oversized playing cards for a chance to win cash. One contestant guesses how many people (out of 100) gave a certain answer to a question and the other contestant then guesses if the number is higher or lower than the opponent's guess. The winning contestant then faces a row of cards and must determine if each succeeding card is higher or lower than the one that precedes it. The contestant who wins two out of three games wins the match and plays the bonus round, called Money Cards. The Money Cards round is similar to the card game in the main game but with three levels of cards instead of one row. The contestant is given $200 at the beginning of Money Cards and wagers any or all of that money when guessing if the cards will be higher or lower than the previous one. A perfect round could earn the contestant $28,800.

programme.title: The Price Is Right
programme.desc: "Come on down!" "The Price Is Right" -- hosted by Bob Barker until 2007 and Drew Carey thereafter -- features a wide variety of games and contests with the same basic challenge: Guess the prices of everyday (or not-quite-everyday) retail items. Four contestants, all of whom are seated in one of the wildest audiences in daytime game-show history, are called to the stage to play a preliminary pricing round. That winner joins the host on stage for one of more than 70 different pricing games. After three such games, the contestants spin a big wheel -- hoping to get as close to $1 as possible -- in the "Showcase Showdown." The two highest winners of that round advance to the final, where prizes could be cars or roomsful of furniture. A trio of models presents the prizes.

programme.title: Card Sharks
programme.desc: This show from legendary Mark Goodson-Bill Todman Productions features two contestants trying to predict answers to survey questions for the opportunity to play a game with oversized playing cards for a chance to win cash. One contestant guesses how many people (out of 100) gave a certain answer to a question and the other contestant then guesses if the number is higher or lower than the opponent's guess. The winning contestant then faces a row of cards and must determine if each succeeding card is higher or lower than the one that precedes it. The contestant who wins two out of three games wins the match and plays the bonus round, called Money Cards. The Money Cards round is similar to the card game in the main game but with three levels of cards instead of one row. The contestant is given $200 at the beginning of Money Cards and wagers any or all of that money when guessing if the cards will be higher or lower than the previous one. A perfect round could earn the contestant $28,800.

programme.title: Mom and Dad Save the World
programme.desc: While planning to destroy Earth with a gigantic laser beam, Emperor Tod Spengo (Jon Lovitz), ruler of the planet Spengo, catches a glimpse of housewife Marge Nelson (Teri Garr) and becomes smitten with her. Beaming Marge and her husband, Dick (Jeffrey Jones), up to Spengo from California, the daft, dimwitted leader tries to woo her, and sends her spouse to prison. Soon Dick is plotting an insurgency, in hopes of overthrowing Spengo and rescuing his wife.

programme.title: They All Laughed
programme.desc: The employees of New York City's Odyssey Detective Agency can't seem to prevent themselves from getting over-involved in their clients' lives. When aging gumshoe John Russo (Ben Gazzara) is assigned to trail an Italian millionaire's wife, Angela (Audrey Hepburn), he inevitably falls for her continental charm. His partner, Charles (John Ritter), is similarly unable to keep his hands off the woman he's trailing -- a winsome cheating spouse named Dolores (Dorothy Stratten).

programme.title: MacGruber

Hap's failings on stage, however, leave them in need of another job: working for a con man (Lloyd Corrigan) who bottles tap water. Durant takes the case, and, with the help of Gazotti and Gertie (Myrna Loy), the victim's roommate, he determines that crime boss Jim Crelliman (C. Henry Gordon) played a role in the murder.
